reason: The quote and ordering are exact: AirdropSpawnGoal.java:265 calls the void spawnAirdropMobs(...) and :266 increments airdropsDone unconditionally, while WaveManager.java:982/983/989 return without any signal to the caller, and the only other write to the field is the constructor reset at AirdropSpawnGoal.java:64 (grep over src/main confirms no setter or reset path). The max check is a per-instance field read at AirdropSpawnGoal.java:73, and the instance is constructed once per spawned dropper at WaveManager.java:697, so the budget is per-dropper, not per-wave; since every wave mob is registered in activeMobs (WaveManager.java:704) and activeMobs must be empty for isWaveCleared() (WaveManager.java:905-911), a dropper normally lives only within one wave, which weakens 'lifetime' to 'this wave'. Reachability of the refusal is real: shouldActivate() gates on isMobCapReached() at line 91 before the flight, and the batch task at WaveManager.java:993-1005 spawns one mob per 10 ticks, so the cap can fill during approach and toSpawn becomes 0 at :988-989. Severity is nevertheless overstated: the mis-accounting fails safe (it can only reduce spawning, never exceed the cap), the dropper deliberately retains DropperAttackGoal harassment (WaveManager.java:702), and repeated no-op burns are largely self-limiting because after a refusal line 91 blocks any new attempt while the cap remains full, so further increments require the cap to be freed and refilled during three separate later flights.
